searches.query: Pollachi Valparai ghat road landslide boulders vehicles stranded
searches.answer: Traffic on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road was disrupted by a landslide that brought down massive boulders and uprooted trees, causing significant damage to the road and leaving motorists and tourists stranded. The landslide occurred around 8 pm on Tuesday, near the third hairpin bend on the road. The road was closed for nearly 20 hours, reopening around 5 pm on Wednesday after extensive efforts to clear the debris. During the closure, tourists and residents faced difficulties, including shortages of food and water. The road was reopened with restrictions, allowing only local residents, government employees, and government buses to use it, while tourist vehicles were barred from entering the Valparai region. The state highways department indicated that permanent repairs and the removal of remaining boulders would take additional time due to ongoing rain and difficult terrain.

# Tamil Nadu: Pollachi-Valparai ghat road reopens after 15-hours following landslide

Incessant and heavy rainfall and strong winds in the Western Ghats, triggered by the northeast monsoon, are believed to have contributed to the incident.

Updated on:

2 min read

* Copied

COIMBATORE: Traffic on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road was partially restored on Wednesday afternoon, nearly 15 hours after a landslide brought down massive boulders and uprooted trees, damaging the road and disrupting movement along the hill route.

The landslide occurred around 8 pm on Tuesday near the second bend below Attakatti, between the second and third hairpin bends on the ghar road connecting Pollachi with Valparai which has a total of 40 hairpin bends. Incessant and heavy rainfall and strong winds in the Western Ghats, triggered by the northeast monsoon, are believed to have contributed to the incident.

Two massive boulders rolled onto the road, causing a major crack in the tarred surface and making the stretch impassable. Uprooted trees also fell across the road, further obstructing traffic. The incident left motorists stranded, while tourists and other travellers faced difficulties, with some reportedly struggling to access food and drinking water.

Following the disruption, vehicles travelling from Pollachi towards Valparai were turned back at the Aliyar forest checkpost.

Those coming from Valparai towards Pollachi were stopped at Attakatti by forest personnel.

State Highways Department officials, revenue officials, police personnel and other departments launched clearance and restoration operations using earthmovers and other machines. Pollachi Sub-Collector Ramakrishnasamy inspected the affected stretch and instructed officials to expedite the work.

Officials said the major portions of the fallen boulders had been broken into smaller pieces and removed before the damaged road was temporarily repaired. Sandbags and barricades have been placed along the affected stretch as a safety measure.

Although traffic resumed on Wednesday afternoon, restrictions remain in force. Only local residents, government employees and government buses are currently permitted to use the ghat road, while tourist vehicles have been barred from entering the Valparai region.

The state highways department officials said removing the remaining boulders and completing permanent repairs would take additional time, given the continuing rain and difficult terrain. They said that the clearance work could be completed within the next couple of days.

![Heavy rains trigger landslide on Valparai ghat road](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-135099366,imgsize-95835,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/valparai-landslidejpg.jpg "Valparai landslide")

Valparai landslide

Coimbatore: A landslide triggered by heavy rain on Tuesday night brought traffic on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road to a halt for nearly 20 hours, leaving scores of tourists and residents of the hill town stranded.Govt officials said two massive boulders rolled onto the road near the third hairpin bend around 8pm, damaging a portion of the stretch. The road, the key link between Pollachi and Valparai, was cleared only around 5pm on Wednesday. No vehicle was passing by when the landslide occurred, averting an accident.A district administration official said personnel from the highways department, police and fire and rescue services worked through the night to clear the boulders. Initial attempts to remove them using earthmovers failed, forcing officials to use rock drills to break them into smaller pieces.The closure left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, without food or water supply at the spot. “We had no alternative road and had to wait throughout the night without food and water until the road was cleared,” said a tourist from Hosur. The disruption also affected the movement of essential supplies, including milk.Though rest of the western region too received intermittent showers, officials said there was no untoward incidents.In Cauvery delta region, Mayiladuthurai received heavy rains while neighbouring Thanjavur and Tiruvarur received moderate showers, offering a relief to farmers who have raised paddy crops.“The downpours have wetted the fields, providing temporary respite. The fields are irrigated for now, and the crops can survive wilting for a couple of weeks” said S Ramadoss, a farmer-representative from Nagapattinam.About 10 lakh acres of samba and thaladi paddy are under cultivation across nine central districts.Samba paddy, roughly six weeks old, is in the tillering and stem elongation stages, while thaladi crops—raised after the kuruvai harvest—are two to three weeks old and still in the seedling stage. Agriculture minister R Vinoth said irrigation channels are being desilted to aid draining of flood waters from fields.As of Oct 21, water level at Mettur dam stood at 54ft against the full reservoir level of 120ft, with storage at just 21tmcft out of the total capacity of 93.4tmcft. The inflow stands at 4,834 cusecs, while outflow was reduced to 6,003 cusecs.Down south, Madurai received negligible rain but weather experts have forecast heavy to very heavy rain on Thursday. The warning extends to Theni, Dindigul, Virudhunagar, Tenkasi, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari.Meanwhile, water levels in reservoirs continued to increase. Vaigai dam rose to 44.88ft now from 43ft last Wednesday, while Mullaperiyar reached 116.90ft.
Papanasam rose to 48 feet from 45.70ft in last one week, and Perunchani reached 44.35ft from 41.97ft, govt data showed.

results.title: Rain triggers minor landslip on Valparai Road - The Hindu
results.content:
A minor landslip occurred on the rain-drenched ghat section of Pollachi–Valparai Road late on Tuesday (October 20), disrupting traffic along the stretch for almost 12 hours.

The landslip was reported near the first hairpin bend of the ghat section around 10.30 p.m., when boulders got dislodged from the slope and slipped onto the road, carrying debris.

12 injured as van carrying tourists topple on Valparai ghat section

Forest Department staff attached to the Pollachi range received information from locals and immediately alerted the Police, Revenue and Highways Departments and the Fire and Rescue Services. [...] Since the ghat section passes through the forests of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve and vehicle movement is restricted between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries.

Motorists warned of increased movement of wild animals on Valparai Road in summer

As vehicles of Valparai residents and those used for emergency services are permitted during night hours, staff stationed at Aliyar checkpost stopped vehicles heading uphill towards Valparai. Similarly, vehicles heading towards Aliyar were stopped at Attakatti checkpost.

The boulders were broken up using a jackhammer attached to the backhoe of an earthmover. The debris on the road was removed and traffic was restored by 9.30 a.m. on Wednesday.

# Rain triggers minor landslip on Valparai Road

## Since vehicle movement is restricted on the ghat section between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries

Published - October 21, 2026 08:04 pm IST - COIMBATORE

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/)

[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)  Remove

An earthmover being used to break up boulders in the debris of a landslip near the first hairpin bend on Pollachi-Valparai Road.

A minor landslip occurred on the rain-drenched ghat section of Pollachi–Valparai Road late on Tuesday (October 20), disrupting traffic along the stretch for almost 12 hours.

The landslip was reported near the first hairpin bend of the ghat section around 10.30 p.m., when boulders got dislodged from the slope and slipped onto the road, carrying debris.

[12 injured as van carrying tourists topple on Valparai ghat section](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/12-injured-as-van-carrying-tourists-topple-on-valparai-ghat-section/article71357304.ece)

![](https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png)

Forest Department staff attached to the Pollachi range received information from locals and immediately alerted the Police, Revenue and Highways Departments and the Fire and Rescue Services.

Since the ghat section passes through the forests of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve and [vehicle movement is restricted](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Coimbatore/forest-department-tightens-time-restriction-on-tourist-vehicles-to-valparai/article67255743.ece) between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries.

[Motorists warned of increased movement of wild animals on Valparai Road in summer](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Coimbatore/motorists-warned-of-increased-movement-of-wild-animals-on-valparai-road-in-summer/article70772741.ece)

![](https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png)

As vehicles of Valparai residents and those used for emergency services are permitted during night hours, staff stationed at Aliyar checkpost stopped vehicles heading uphill towards Valparai. Similarly, vehicles heading towards Aliyar were stopped at Attakatti checkpost.

The boulders were broken up using a jackhammer attached to the backhoe of an earthmover. The debris on the road was removed and traffic was restored by 9.30 a.m. on Wednesday.

Published - October 21, 2026 08:04 pm IST

The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water.

COIMBATORE: Heavy rain on Tuesday night triggered a landslide, sending massive boulders rolling onto the Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road and bringing traffic to a standstill for more than 15 hours, leaving scores of tourists and commuters stranded. The disruption continued into Wednesday, with officials deploying heavy machinery to remove the boulders and restore traffic.The landslide occurred near the third hairpin bend on the ghat road around 8pm on Tuesday, with two giant boulders rolling onto the carriageway and damaging a section of the road. The impact left the stretch impassable even for two-wheelers, cutting off the main road link between Pollachi and Valparai. No vehicles were passing at the time of the incident, averting a possible major accident. The road was cleared around 5pm on Wednesday, after almost 21 hours.According to an official from the district administration, the size of the boulders made their removal difficult. The official said, “Because of the size, personnel from the highways department, police and fire and rescue services had to carry out work throughout the night.We could not allow vehicle movement until the road was cleared, considering the safety of passengers. Initially, we attempted to remove the boulders with earthmovers but failed. So, we had to use rock drills to make them small pieces and then remove them.”The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water. Families with children were among those stranded near the Aliyar checkpost.Vehicles travelling uphill from Pollachi were stopped, while those descending from Valparai were held back until the road could be cleared.A tourist from Hosur said, “My three friends and I came to Valparai on Monday and were returning on Tuesday night. We had no alternative road and had to wait until the road was cleared. District officials could have provided some assistance, at least to provide water or food for those waiting throughout the night. More than 100 people have been left stranded including children and families.”The road closure affected the movement of essential supplies, including milk.
Aliyar recorded 96.8mm of rain until Wednesday morning, according to the Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Authority’s report. Coimbatore district received a cumulative 523 mm of rainfall.

The rally was driven by strong performance in iron ore, electricity, coal, refinery products, cement and steel

NEW DELHI: India's core sector growth accelerated to 7.9 per cent in September 2026, up from 5.9 per cent in August, driven by strong output across six of the eight key infrastructure industries, according to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday.The Index of Eight Core Industries (ICI) tracks the performance of coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. These industries account for 40.27 per cent of the weight of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), making the index an important indicator of industrial activity.Iron ore production recorded the highest year-on-year growth at 18.4 per cent in September, followed by electricity at 11.4 per cent and coal at 10.7 per cent. Refinery products grew 10.3 per cent, cement output increased 9.8 per cent, while steel production rose 4.9 per cent during the month.In contrast, fertiliser production declined 11.7 per cent in September, while natural gas output contracted 4.6 per cent and crude oil production fell 1.4 per cent year-on-year.Coal, refinery products, steel and iron ore have been the major drivers of overall core sector growth in recent months, the ministry said.The cumulative growth rate of the core industries index stood at 5.1 per cent during April-September 2026, compared with 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, according to provisional data.The ministry also revised the final index for August 2026 upwards to 120.4 from the provisional estimate of 119.2. Consequently, the year-on-year growth rate for August was revised to 5.9 per cent from the earlier estimate of 4.8 per cent.The September 2026 figures are provisional. The ministry said the index for October 2026 is scheduled to be released on November 20.

# Taurus Horoscope Tomorrow, October 22, 2026: Pisces Moon Square Uranus Brings Sudden News in Money

[![](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/authorphoto/479269904.cms)](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-Neeraj-Dhankher-479269904.cms)[Neeraj Dhankher](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-Neeraj-Dhankher-479269904.cms) / TOI Astrology /  Oct 21, 2026, 16:45 IST

Comments

Share

Aa

**Text Size**

* Small
* Medium
* Large

[Print](/articleshowprint/134995393.cms "print article")

A message about money arrives when you least expect it. The Moon in Pisces, in your 11th house of networks, gains and group plans, forms a square with Uranus in Gemini, your 2nd house of income, savings and spending. Mutable signs pull in different directions. A contact’s news and your own budget may not agree. So check the figure before you act on the feeling.

## Taurus Career Predictions

A contact or teammate may pass on news about a payment, a rate or a new lead. It may change the week's plan. Ask who confirmed it and by when. A senior could hear about it before you do, so keep your notes ready. Group tasks need dates and names. And get any change in pay terms by email.

[Watch

You Are on Jupiter's Lucky List? Aries to Pisces: Who Benefits Most from it ?|Ft. Prakash Joshi](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/lifestyle/mantra/you-are-on-jupiters-lucky-list-aries-to-pisces-who-benefits-most-from-it-ft-prakash-joshi/videoshow/131477804.cms)

## Taurus Love Predictions

A friend’s remark about money or plans may reach a partner and cause a small stir. Explain calmly, without defending every word. Couples can clear it with one direct question. Singles may hear of someone through a group message. Interest looks lively but uncertain. Let a few chats pass before you plan a meeting.

## Taurus Money Predictions

A sudden fee, a refund or a surprise offer may appear through a message or a group. Uranus favours quick moves, so verify the source and the amount first.Do not pay on a forwarded link. A small gain is possible, but it may come late. So spend only against what has landed, and keep the proof.

## Taurus Health Predictions

Surprise news may tighten the throat, neck and stomach, and sleep could be uneven. Eat plain meals at regular hours. Sip warm water. Calves and ankles may feel slow after a busy social day. And leave group chats unread for the last hour of the evening, since the mind needs a gap to settle.

## Taurus Remedies

Check one money message twice before you act on it. Take an easy walk outdoors after dinner.

results.title: Rain batters Nilgiris; landslide buries government bus, driver loses life
results.content:
She urged tourists to avoid visiting the Nilgiris for the next three days. The district administration has suspended the movement of all vehicles, including TNSTC buses, between 6 pm and 7 am for three days, exempting ambulances and other essential vehicles.

Similar instructions have been issued for Valparai. The Railways has cancelled train services between Mettupalayam and Udhagamandalam on the Nilgiris Mountain Railway for two days following multiple landslides.

A driver travelling in an empty poultry van was also stranded after his vehicle reportedly plunged into a 100-foot gorge during the landslide. He escaped unhurt and returned home.

Parts of Kodaikanal cut off [...] Rescue personnel from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) and the Fire and Rescue Services Department rescued Kesavan around 7.30 am on Saturday. Janagaraj was found dead around 11.10 am. He is suspected to have died from a head injury. The bus was severely damaged, with debris entering the vehicle and trapping the two occupants. Rescue teams could not reach the spot immediately as fallen trees and landslide debris blocked the road. They began the operation around 5 am after clearing the obstructions.

Meanwhile, 241 students and 25 teachers from Kerala, who were on a trip to Ooty, were stranded in seven buses due to the disruption of traffic on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road.

Chennai may receive moderate to heavy rain; red alert issued for Dindigul, Theni, Madurai [...] Rescue personnel helped them reach safety, and they were accommodated at marriage halls and a school in Mettupalayam and Kallar. Stranded passengers and drivers were also provided food and medical assistance.

Minister for Backward Classes V Sampath Kumar said the students had been rescued and could retrieve their vehicles once the road was restored and the rain subsided. # Rain batters Nilgiris; landslide buries government bus, driver loses life

241 students and 25 teachers from Kerala, who were on a trip to Ooty, were stranded in seven buses due to the disruption of traffic on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road. 

TNDRF personnel engaging in rescue operations to recover the bus caught in a landslide in Burliyar on Saturday Photo | S Senbagapandiyan

[S Senthil Kumar](/author/s-senthil-kumar)

Updated on:

4 min read

* Copied

COIMBATORE: A TNSTC bus driver was killed and the conductor was rescued after being trapped for more than eight hours when a landslide buried their vehicle at Burliyar on the Coonoor-Mettupalayam ghat road in the Nilgiris on Friday night. All 40 passengers had alighted earlier after the bus developed a flat tyre.

The driver, J Janagaraj (51) of Katteri dam, and conductor Kesavan (34) of Solur Mattam in Kil Kotagiri were looking for a suitable place to stop after the tyre went flat. The bus was travelling from Coonoor to Coimbatore when a tree fell across the road, forcing the driver to reverse. Another tree fell around 10.30 pm, further restricting their movement, before a landslide sent trees, rocks and silt crashing down on the vehicle.

“The driver reversed the bus for some distance after we were unable to proceed because a tree had fallen across the road. However, another tree fell across the road at 10.30 pm, further restricting our movement. I noticed rainwater flowing down the hillside when the landslide occurred,” Kesavan said. He is undergoing treatment at the Mettupalayam Government Hospital.

Rescue personnel from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) and the Fire and Rescue Services Department rescued Kesavan around 7.30 am on Saturday. Janagaraj was found dead around 11.10 am. He is suspected to have died from a head injury. The bus was severely damaged, with debris entering the vehicle and trapping the two occupants. Rescue teams could not reach the spot immediately as fallen trees and landslide debris blocked the road. They began the operation around 5 am after clearing the obstructions.

Meanwhile, 241 students and 25 teachers from Kerala, who were on a trip to Ooty, were stranded in seven buses due to the disruption of traffic on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road.

**Chennai may receive moderate to heavy rain; red alert issued for Dindigul, Theni, Madurai**

Rescue personnel helped them reach safety, and they were accommodated at marriage halls and a school in Mettupalayam and Kallar. Stranded passengers and drivers were also provided food and medical assistance.

Minister for Backward Classes V Sampath Kumar said the students had been rescued and could retrieve their vehicles once the road was restored and the rain subsided. Later on Saturday evening, the Kerala students were sent back to their native places in buses. Stranded passengers and drivers were also provided with food and medical assistance. Animal Husbandry Minister S Kamali also monitored the rescue and relief work.

Coimbatore Collector Pavankumar G Giriyappanavar said police, revenue, local body and State Highways personnel assisted rescue teams from Mettupalayam, Coonoor, Periyanaickenpalayam, Annur, Kavundampalayam and Sulur.

**IMD alerts, restrictions and wider impact**

The Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai has forecast heavy rain in TN until Monday, as a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a cyclonic storm.

It is very likely to move further northwestwards, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross Andhra Pradesh​ and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam ​by forenoon of October 28. Burliyar in the Nilgiris recorded 25 cm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Saturday, the highest in the state during the period.

Kil Kotagiri Estate received 20 cm, Coonoor 17 cm, Mettupalayam 15 cm and Kotagiri 14 cm. According to TN-SMART data, Virugavoor in the Kallakurichi district recorded a 20 cm of rainfall on Saturday night, while surrounding interior districts registered a lower baseline average of 6.8 mm.

Localised stations within Tiruvannamalai, such as Chengam, separately logged rainfall as high as 11.16 cm. The IMD has issued a red alert for Theni, Dindigul and Madurai districts for Sunday, with extremely heavy rain likely at isolated places. An orange alert is in force for the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Karur, Tiruchy, Nagapattinam, Ariyalur, Perambalur, Sivaganga, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Pudukkottai. Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram and Sivaganga are also under an orange alert for Monday.

Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph are likely at isolated places across TN, Puducherry and Karaikal till Monday. Chennai is likely to receive moderate to heavy rain with thunderstorms on Sunday.

The downpour triggered landslides at 19 locations and tree falls at 18 locations across the Nilgiris. The incident has revived memories of the 1993 Marapalam landslide, when two buses were reportedly buried, killing passengers.

Following the landslides and tree falls, Nilgiris Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Taneeru announced that tourist spots in the district would remain closed until further orders.

She urged tourists to avoid visiting the Nilgiris for the next three days. The district administration has suspended the movement of all vehicles, including TNSTC buses, between 6 pm and 7 am for three days, exempting ambulances and other essential vehicles.

Similar instructions have been issued for Valparai. The Railways has cancelled train services between Mettupalayam and Udhagamandalam on the Nilgiris Mountain Railway for two days following multiple landslides.

A driver travelling in an empty poultry van was also stranded after his vehicle reportedly plunged into a 100-foot gorge during the landslide. He escaped unhurt and returned home.

**Parts of Kodaikanal cut off**

Heavy rain brought parts of Kodaikanal to a standstill on Friday and Saturday, with landslides reported at several locations in Dindigul district. Adukkam panchayat, along the Periyakulam-Kodaikanal route, was cut off after landslides damaged the road at seven locations.

The district administration ordered the closure of tourist spots in Dindigul on Sunday.

A State Highways Department official said the stretch connecting Periyakulam in Theni district and Kodaikanal through Adukkam suffered extensive damage and was closed to traffic on Friday.

Representational purpose

[Express News Service](/author/express-news-service)

Updated on:

2 min read

* Copied

COIMBATORE: Traffic on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road was partially restored on Wednesday afternoon, nearly 15 hours after a landslide brought down massive boulders and uprooted trees, damaging the road and disrupting movement along the hill route.

The landslide occurred around 8 pm on Tuesday near the second bend below Attakatti, between the second and third hairpin bends on the ghar road connecting Pollachi with Valparai which has a total of 40 hairpin bends. Incessant and heavy rainfall and strong winds in the Western Ghats, triggered by the northeast monsoon, are believed to have contributed to the incident.

Two massive boulders rolled onto the road, causing a major crack in the tarred surface and making the stretch impassable. Uprooted trees also fell across the road, further obstructing traffic. The incident left motorists stranded, while tourists and other travellers faced difficulties, with some reportedly struggling to access food and drinking water.

Following the disruption, vehicles travelling from Pollachi towards Valparai were turned back at the Aliyar forest checkpost.

Those coming from Valparai towards Pollachi were stopped at Attakatti by forest personnel.

State Highways Department officials, revenue officials, police personnel and other departments launched clearance and restoration operations using earthmovers and other machines. Pollachi Sub-Collector Ramakrishnasamy inspected the affected stretch and instructed officials to expedite the work.

Officials said the major portions of the fallen boulders had been broken into smaller pieces and removed before the damaged road was temporarily repaired. Sandbags and barricades have been placed along the affected stretch as a safety measure.

Although traffic resumed on Wednesday afternoon, restrictions remain in force. Only local residents, government employees and government buses are currently permitted to use the ghat road, while tourist vehicles have been barred from entering the Valparai region.

The state highways department officials said removing the remaining boulders and completing permanent repairs would take additional time, given the continuing rain and difficult terrain. They said that the clearance work could be completed within the next couple of days.

PHULABANI: A month-long closure of Kalinga Ghat on National Highway-157 has disrupted life along the Kandhamal-Ganjam border, pushing up the cost of essential commodities, crippling roadside businesses and forcing commuters and goods carriers to take a detour of around 50 km.

Amid growing public resentment over the delay in restoring traffic, a three-member team of experts from IIT Delhi inspected the landslide-affected stretches on Sunday to recommend a permanent solution. The closure followed landslides triggered by incessant rainfall, including a massive boulder fall at the spot where the road had remained blocked for 47 days last year.

The falling rock damaged the road and guard walls on both sides. Road-widening work near Andharakote also collapsed, further complicating restoration. The prolonged disruption has increased transportation costs, adding to the burden on consumers already struggling with rising prices.

Tea stalls, hotels, roadside eateries and restaurants in Durgaprasad and Kalinga Ghat have reportedly shut down due to the sharp decline in traffic and customers, leaving hundreds of families dependent on these businesses facing financial hardship.

The expert team comprising IIT Delhi professors G V Raman, Prashant Bhangla and Sumit Sinha, accompanied by locals officials, visited Kalinga Ghat to assess the condition of the affected slopes, examine the possible causes of the landslides and suggest measures to minimise future risks.

HMBS Textiles Pvt Ltd has been entrusted with work related to the proposed intervention. The experts will prepare a technical report and submit recommendations to the authorities. The inspection assumes significance as residents continue to question the delay in reopening the highway. Although the large boulder that fell this year was removed within two days, and some rocks lodged higher up the hillside were subsequently blasted, traffic remains suspended.

The proposed project envisages road widening, landslide-risk mitigation measures and reconstruction of a minor culvert. An innovative reinforced earth composite or hybrid system has been proposed as part of the engineering intervention. The measures are aimed at addressing the vulnerabilities of the stretch and improving its long-term stability.

# Heavy rains trigger landslide on Valparai ghat road

Times News Network/  Oct 22, 2026, 00:16 IST

![Heavy rains trigger landslide on Valparai ghat road](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-135099366,imgsize-95835,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/valparai-landslidejpg.jpg "Valparai landslide")

Valparai landslide

Coimbatore: A landslide triggered by heavy rain on Tuesday night brought traffic on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road to a halt for nearly 20 hours, leaving scores of tourists and residents of the hill town stranded.Govt officials said two massive boulders rolled onto the road near the third hairpin bend around 8pm, damaging a portion of the stretch. The road, the key link between Pollachi and Valparai, was cleared only around 5pm on Wednesday. No vehicle was passing by when the landslide occurred, averting an accident.A district administration official said personnel from the highways department, police and fire and rescue services worked through the night to clear the boulders. Initial attempts to remove them using earthmovers failed, forcing officials to use rock drills to break them into smaller pieces.The closure left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, without food or water supply at the spot. “We had no alternative road and had to wait throughout the night without food and water until the road was cleared,” said a tourist from Hosur. The disruption also affected the movement of essential supplies, including milk.Though rest of the western region too received intermittent showers, officials said there was no untoward incidents.In Cauvery delta region, Mayiladuthurai received heavy rains while neighbouring Thanjavur and Tiruvarur received moderate showers, offering a relief to farmers who have raised paddy crops.“The downpours have wetted the fields, providing temporary respite. The fields are irrigated for now, and the crops can survive wilting for a couple of weeks” said S Ramadoss, a farmer-representative from Nagapattinam.About 10 lakh acres of samba and thaladi paddy are under cultivation across nine central districts.Samba paddy, roughly six weeks old, is in the tillering and stem elongation stages, while thaladi crops—raised after the kuruvai harvest—are two to three weeks old and still in the seedling stage. Agriculture minister R Vinoth said irrigation channels are being desilted to aid draining of flood waters from fields.As of Oct 21, water level at Mettur dam stood at 54ft against the full reservoir level of 120ft, with storage at just 21tmcft out of the total capacity of 93.4tmcft. The inflow stands at 4,834 cusecs, while outflow was reduced to 6,003 cusecs.Down south, Madurai received negligible rain but weather experts have forecast heavy to very heavy rain on Thursday. The warning extends to Theni, Dindigul, Virudhunagar, Tenkasi, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari.Meanwhile, water levels in reservoirs continued to increase. Vaigai dam rose to 44.88ft now from 43ft last Wednesday, while Mullaperiyar reached 116.90ft.
Papanasam rose to 48 feet from 45.70ft in last one week, and Perunchani reached 44.35ft from 41.97ft, govt data showed.

results.title: Rain triggers minor landslip on Valparai Road - The Hindu
results.content:
A minor landslip occurred on the rain-drenched ghat section of Pollachi–Valparai Road late on Tuesday (October 20), disrupting traffic along the stretch for almost 12 hours.

The landslip was reported near the first hairpin bend of the ghat section around 10.30 p.m., when boulders got dislodged from the slope and slipped onto the road, carrying debris.

12 injured as van carrying tourists topple on Valparai ghat section

Forest Department staff attached to the Pollachi range received information from locals and immediately alerted the Police, Revenue and Highways Departments and the Fire and Rescue Services. [...] Since the ghat section passes through the forests of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve and vehicle movement is restricted between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries.

Motorists warned of increased movement of wild animals on Valparai Road in summer

As vehicles of Valparai residents and those used for emergency services are permitted during night hours, staff stationed at Aliyar checkpost stopped vehicles heading uphill towards Valparai. Similarly, vehicles heading towards Aliyar were stopped at Attakatti checkpost.

The boulders were broken up using a jackhammer attached to the backhoe of an earthmover. The debris on the road was removed and traffic was restored by 9.30 a.m. on Wednesday.

# Rain triggers minor landslip on Valparai Road

## Since vehicle movement is restricted on the ghat section between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries

Published - October 21, 2026 08:04 pm IST - COIMBATORE

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/)

[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)  Remove

An earthmover being used to break up boulders in the debris of a landslip near the first hairpin bend on Pollachi-Valparai Road.

A minor landslip occurred on the rain-drenched ghat section of Pollachi–Valparai Road late on Tuesday (October 20), disrupting traffic along the stretch for almost 12 hours.

The landslip was reported near the first hairpin bend of the ghat section around 10.30 p.m., when boulders got dislodged from the slope and slipped onto the road, carrying debris.

[12 injured as van carrying tourists topple on Valparai ghat section](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/12-injured-as-van-carrying-tourists-topple-on-valparai-ghat-section/article71357304.ece)

![](https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png)

Forest Department staff attached to the Pollachi range received information from locals and immediately alerted the Police, Revenue and Highways Departments and the Fire and Rescue Services.

Since the ghat section passes through the forests of the Anamalai Tiger Reserve and [vehicle movement is restricted](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Coimbatore/forest-department-tightens-time-restriction-on-tourist-vehicles-to-valparai/article67255743.ece) between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m., the landslip did not result in human casualties or injuries.

[Motorists warned of increased movement of wild animals on Valparai Road in summer](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Coimbatore/motorists-warned-of-increased-movement-of-wild-animals-on-valparai-road-in-summer/article70772741.ece)

![](https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png)

As vehicles of Valparai residents and those used for emergency services are permitted during night hours, staff stationed at Aliyar checkpost stopped vehicles heading uphill towards Valparai. Similarly, vehicles heading towards Aliyar were stopped at Attakatti checkpost.

The boulders were broken up using a jackhammer attached to the backhoe of an earthmover. The debris on the road was removed and traffic was restored by 9.30 a.m. on Wednesday.

[![](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/authorphoto/479263631.cms)](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-anushka-juliet-479263631.cms)[Anushka Juliet](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-anushka-juliet-479263631.cms) / TNN /  Oct 21, 2026, 18:45 IST

![Tourists, commuters stranded as landslide disrupts traffic on Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road for several hours](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-135093412,imgsize-144424,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/valparai_landslide.jpg "The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water.")

The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water.

COIMBATORE: Heavy rain on Tuesday night triggered a landslide, sending massive boulders rolling onto the Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road and bringing traffic to a standstill for more than 15 hours, leaving scores of tourists and commuters stranded. The disruption continued into Wednesday, with officials deploying heavy machinery to remove the boulders and restore traffic.The landslide occurred near the third hairpin bend on the ghat road around 8pm on Tuesday, with two giant boulders rolling onto the carriageway and damaging a section of the road. The impact left the stretch impassable even for two-wheelers, cutting off the main road link between Pollachi and Valparai. No vehicles were passing at the time of the incident, averting a possible major accident. The road was cleared around 5pm on Wednesday, after almost 21 hours.According to an official from the district administration, the size of the boulders made their removal difficult. The official said, “Because of the size, personnel from the highways department, police and fire and rescue services had to carry out work throughout the night.We could not allow vehicle movement until the road was cleared, considering the safety of passengers. Initially, we attempted to remove the boulders with earthmovers but failed. So, we had to use rock drills to make them small pieces and then remove them.”The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water. Families with children were among those stranded near the Aliyar checkpost.Vehicles travelling uphill from Pollachi were stopped, while those descending from Valparai were held back until the road could be cleared.A tourist from Hosur said, “My three friends and I came to Valparai on Monday and were returning on Tuesday night. We had no alternative road and had to wait until the road was cleared. District officials could have provided some assistance, at least to provide water or food for those waiting throughout the night. More than 100 people have been left stranded including children and families.”The road closure affected the movement of essential supplies, including milk.
Aliyar recorded 96.8mm of rain until Wednesday morning, according to the Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Authority’s report. Coimbatore district received a cumulative 523 mm of rainfall.

images.description: Tourists, commuters stranded as landslide disrupts traffic on Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road for several hours

results.title: All tourist spots in Nilgiris closed due to red alert for heavy rain - The Hindu
results.content:
In a separate public safety advisory issued on Saturday, the Coimbatore district administration said the public should avoid the ghat roads from Mettupalayam to Udhagamandalam via Coonoor and Kotagiri, and from Pollachi to Valparai, as major landslides had occurred at several locations.

Vehicle movement, including Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus services, to the Nilgiris and Valparai has been stopped between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. Essential and emergency vehicles are exempt from the restriction. [...] The Hindu Bureau

SEE ALL  Remove

All tourist spots in the Nilgiris district have been ordered to remain closed until further notice, while the Coimbatore district administration has advised the public to avoid ghat roads connecting Mettupalayam with Udhagamandalam and Pollachi with Valparai, following heavy rain and landslides at several locations.

The Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru ordered the closure of tourist spots on Saturday (October 24) after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for very heavy rainfall in the district on October 24 and 25. In a press release, she said heavy rain had resulted in trees falling across roads and landslides, disrupting traffic. [...] Brandhub

# All tourist spots in Nilgiris closed due to red alert for heavy rain

## Coimbatore district administration tells public to avoid ghat roads from Mettupalayam to Udhagamandalam via Coonoor and Kotagiri, and from Pollachi to Valparai, as major landslides had occurred at several locations

Published - October 24, 2026 07:31 pm IST - Coimbatore

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/)

[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)  Remove

All tourist spots in the Nilgiris district have been ordered to remain closed until further notice, while the Coimbatore district administration has advised the public to avoid ghat roads connecting Mettupalayam with Udhagamandalam and Pollachi with Valparai, following heavy rain and landslides at several locations.

The Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru ordered the closure of tourist spots on Saturday (October 24) after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for very heavy rainfall in the district on October 24 and 25. In a press release, she said heavy rain had resulted in trees falling across roads and landslides, disrupting traffic.

In a separate public safety advisory issued on Saturday, the Coimbatore district administration said the public should avoid the ghat roads from Mettupalayam to Udhagamandalam via Coonoor and Kotagiri, and from Pollachi to Valparai, as major landslides had occurred at several locations.

Vehicle movement, including Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus services, to the Nilgiris and Valparai has been stopped between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. Essential and emergency vehicles are exempt from the restriction.

The administration has cautioned that heavy rain could result in trees falling across roads, landslides, rockfalls and sudden flooding. The public has been advised against visiting waterfalls, rivers, streams, dams, lakes and other water bodies, and asked to stay away from flooded roads, overflowing streams and low-lying areas.

People have also been advised to avoid public places and tourist destinations unless necessary, and not to touch electric poles or wires during rain. The administrations have urged the public to follow official advisories and take precautions.

For assistance or to report rain-related damage, the public can contact the District Emergency Operations Centre at the toll-free number 1077 or 0422-2306051. The control room operates round the clock.

# TN's Nilgiris district hit by 62 landslips in 24 hours

The impact of rain over the past couple of days resulted in landslides and landslips at 62 places across the Nilgiris district in the last 24 hours ending at 7 am on Sunday.

The Amanalingeswarar Temple was surrounded by floodwater on Sunday  Photo | Express

[Express News Service](/author/express-news-service)

Updated on:

2 min read

* Copied

**NILGIRIS/COIMBATORE/TIRUPPUR/SALEM:** Two persons were injured and hospitalised after a tree fell on their roof-tiled house in Ooty, as incessant rains lashed the Nilgiris, Coimbatore and other parts of western Tamil Nadu on Sunday. The impact of rain over the past couple of days resulted in landslides and landslips at 62 places across the Nilgiris district in the last 24 hours ending at 7 am on Sunday.

While four tiled-roof houses were also partially damaged in Krishnagiri district, visitors were turned away at Yercaud in Salem district. Devotees were evacuated from the Amanalingeswarar Temple near Thirumoorthy Hills, and tourists were not permitted to take a dip at Panchalinga Falls. Tourists were also not allowed to visit Kodiveri Dam in Gobichettipalayam of Tiruppur district due to flooding in Bhavani River.

In Coimbatore, the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital (CMCH) was also flooded with rainwater, with water entering patients’ wards. A government bus was also stranded in Lanka Corner subway due to inundation. In light of the incessant rain, Coimbatore Collector Pavankumar G Giriyappanavar declared a holiday for all schools across the district on Monday.

Meanwhile, the ban on vehicular movement on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road continued for the second consecutive day on Sunday following a massive landslide at Burliyar that killed a TNSTC bus driver and injured the conductor, who is undergoing treatment at Mettupalayam GH, on Saturday.

With bus services suspended, a group of passengers got into an argument with the police, who explained that the restriction had been imposed in the interest of public safety. After discussions, the authorities arranged accommodation for them on Saturday night. On Sunday morning, they travelled to Coonoor and neighbouring areas via the Kotagiri road.

The rain also affected restoration work. A huge boulder fell between the 13th and 14th hairpin bends on the Valparai Ghat Road, disrupting vehicular movement on Sunday night.

A distribution transformer (DT) and nine electric poles were also damaged in the same period, resulting in power cuts.

# Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds

## The latest floods and landslides have killed at least 24 people and left 14 missing across several districts in Nepal.

* Edited by:  [Prapti Upadhayay](https://www.ndtv.com/authors/prapti-upadhayay-8790)

![Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds](https://c.ndtvimg.com/2026-09/q6gud5t8_nepal_625x300_28_September_26.jpg?im=FeatureCrop,algorithm=dnn,width=773,height=435 "Video: Screams Heard As Part Of Nepal Mountain Crumbles Into River In Seconds")

These events come about a month after the Bhotekoshi floods.

* Two videos show mountainsides collapsing in Nepal amid floods and landslides
* Kali Gandaki River briefly blocked by debris after mountain slide in Mustang District
* Floods and landslides have killed 24 and left 14 missing across multiple districts

[How can authorities prevent future landslide disasters in Nepal?](https://www.ndtv.com/ask?article_id=12109464&redirect_question=How+can+authorities+prevent+future+landslide+disasters+in+Nepal%3F)

In Nepal, two sets of videos from separate places have one thing in common -- each contains six seconds that are hard to watch. In that short time, a mountainside is seen giving way, and the people watching can be heard crying out as it happens.

The first video was shot near Lete in Mustang District, following a fresh spell of floods and landslides on Sunday. It shows a large section of a mountain sliding into the Kali Gandaki River in the valley below within about six seconds. Residents can be heard screaming as the debris rushes downhill. The footage was recorded by Char Dham pilgrims.

> On Camera, Nepal Mountain Melts Into River In Seconds Amid Landslides [pic.twitter.com/wzU4g2kout](https://t.co/wzU4g2kout)
>
> — NDTV (@ndtv) [September 28, 2026](https://x.com/ndtv/status/2104536660625305846?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The river was briefly blocked by the debris before the water cut a path through and began flowing again.

In the second video, shot from a hillside, the ground can be seen giving way and sinking into the valley. Part of a stone-and-wood shelter and several trees are carried down with it. Villagers can be heard screaming as the camera pans, and voices shout "Ghar gai sakyo", which means "the home is already gone". A woman, probably a resident of a house on the steep slope, can be seen crying out in despair.

> "Home Is Already Gone": Nepal Villagers Scream As Hillside Sinks Into Valley [pic.twitter.com/QKyYow44VA](https://t.co/QKyYow44VA)
>
> — NDTV (@ndtv) [September 28, 2026](https://x.com/ndtv/status/2104542533124849779?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Read: [Relentless Rainfall Triggers Floods, Landslides Across Nepal](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/relentless-rainfall-triggers-floods-landslides-across-nepal-12104033)

The latest floods and landslides have killed at least 24 people and left 14 missing across several districts. In Gandaki Province, the Kali Gandaki began rising on Saturday and had become a major flood by Sunday morning, following three days of continuous heavy rain.

The river caused damage from Mustang and Myagdi through Parbat and Syangja, and in one Parbat village it swept away an entire settlement. Landslides have also blocked highways leading to Chitwan and made search and rescue work harder, while security forces have moved thousands of people to safer ground.

Separately, two people were killed, and [10 others remain missing](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/10-missing-after-avalanche-hits-himlung-himal-base-camp-in-nepal-12104067) after an avalanche struck the base camp of [Himlung Himal](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/2-killed-10-missing-after-avalanche-strikes-nepals-himlung-himal-peak-12106461) in Manang district on Sunday, police said. The avalanche hit the Nar Phu area of the 7,126-metre peak and buried a tent where nine climbers and 13 support staff had taken shelter.

These events come about a month after the Bhotekoshi floods, which struck on August 26. Authorities say that the flood has so far claimed more than 1,400 lives and left more than 6,000 people missing.

# Driver dies as TNSTC bus buried under landslide on Mettupalayam-Coonoor Ghat Road during heavy rain

[![](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/authorphoto/479273796.cms)](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-tysion-prabhu-479273796.cms)[Tysion Prabhu](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-tysion-prabhu-479273796.cms) / TNN /  Oct 24, 2026, 21:36 IST

![Driver dies as TNSTC bus buried under landslide on Mettupalayam-Coonoor Ghat Road during heavy rain](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-135173635,imgsize-221136,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/bus_landlside.jpg "The accident happened near Burliar on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor Ghat Road")

The accident happened near Burliar on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor Ghat Road

COIMBATORE: The driver of a Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus died and its conductor sustained fractures after their vehicle was buried by a landslide caused by heavy rain near Burliar on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor Ghat Road late on Friday night.The deceased driver has been identified as Janagaraj, 55, of Katteri near Coonoor. Conductor Kesavan, 38, of Kotagiri was rescued and admitted to Mettupalayam Government Hospital on Saturday.The bus going from Ooty to Coimbatore had suffered a flat tyre near Pudhukkadu in the Nilgiris district, and the passengers numbering around 40 were shifted to another bus. Later, driver Janagaraj and conductor Kesavan were taking the bus to Mettupalayam when torrential rain triggered a landslide around 10pm, burying the vehicle under mounds of earth, boulders and uprooted trees. The landslide happened in Coimbatore district, around 200 metres away from the Nilgiris district border.Six teams from the fire and rescue services from Coimbatore, alongside personnel from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF), were deployed. They battled the difficult terrain through the night to clear the debris. They reached the crushed bus around 5am on Saturday and retrieved Janagaraj’s body and rescued Kesavan."Reaching the site proved arduous due to back-to-back landslides along the eight km stretch," said Coimbatore district collector Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar.Continuous downpours triggered landslides at more than 19 locations on the ghat road. More than 300 people, including students from Kerala who were on a trip to the Nilgiris, were stranded due to the landslides. They were rescued by rescue teams on Saturday morning.Burliar recorded the highest rainfall in the Nilgiris at 250 mm, followed by Kil Kotagiri Estate (200 mm). Vehicular traffic was crippled, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway (NMR) services were cancelled and schools in six taluks remained shut.The Coonoor–Mettupalayam ghat stretch bore the brunt of the devastation, with a critical 7-8 km corridor completely choked with cascading mud, fallen trees, and dislodged boulders. "Rescuers braved active slide zones to clear pathways and shift stranded travellers to a relief camp at a community hall in Mettupalayam,” Giriyappanavar said.For travellers, the ordeal was harrowing. Babu, an omnibus driver ferrying 40 passengers from Ooty to Bengaluru, recounted a terrifying night: "The TNSTC govt bus was right behind us when the hillside caved in. Uprooted trunks blocked our forward path. We spent hours in total darkness amid torrential rain until rescue teams broke through."Saravanan, a truck driver from Mettupalayam, noted that another landslip hit the area shortly after the bus was trapped. "A minitruck tipped into the adjacent gorge. Some fellow drivers and I managed to pull the driver out just in time," he said.On Friday evening, Bhojan, 58, of Sedikkal tribal village near Kotagiri lost his life while he was returning after attending a funeral at Koppaiyur. A swollen mountain stream swept him away. In Theetukal near Ooty, a 100-foot-long, 30-foot-high retaining wall collapsed, flattening two cars and burying six two-wheelers. Emergency personnel pulled watchman Venkatesh, 65, alive from the wreckage.Following inspections by Nilgiris collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru and superintendent of police S Brinda between Burliar and Coonoor, authorities enforced strict restrictions. All tourist destinations in the Nilgiris have been shut until further notice. Vehicular traffic on the ghat corridors -- via both Coonoor and Kotagiri -- remains barred between 6pm and 6am for the next three days. Motorists are advised to postpone all non-essential hill travel.
Animal husbandry minister S Kamali, minister for backward classes V Sampath Kumar, Coimbatore district Collector Pavankumar G Giriyappanavar, inspector general of police (West Zone) RV Ramya Bharathi, Coimbatore district superintendent of police A Pavan Kumar and officials from various departments were involved in the rescue operations.

# Rain batters Nilgiris; landslide buries government bus, driver loses life

241 students and 25 teachers from Kerala, who were on a trip to Ooty, were stranded in seven buses due to the disruption of traffic on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road. 

TNDRF personnel engaging in rescue operations to recover the bus caught in a landslide in Burliyar on Saturday Photo | S Senbagapandiyan

[S Senthil Kumar](/author/s-senthil-kumar)

Updated on:

4 min read

* Copied

COIMBATORE: A TNSTC bus driver was killed and the conductor was rescued after being trapped for more than eight hours when a landslide buried their vehicle at Burliyar on the Coonoor-Mettupalayam ghat road in the Nilgiris on Friday night. All 40 passengers had alighted earlier after the bus developed a flat tyre.

The driver, J Janagaraj (51) of Katteri dam, and conductor Kesavan (34) of Solur Mattam in Kil Kotagiri were looking for a suitable place to stop after the tyre went flat. The bus was travelling from Coonoor to Coimbatore when a tree fell across the road, forcing the driver to reverse. Another tree fell around 10.30 pm, further restricting their movement, before a landslide sent trees, rocks and silt crashing down on the vehicle.

“The driver reversed the bus for some distance after we were unable to proceed because a tree had fallen across the road. However, another tree fell across the road at 10.30 pm, further restricting our movement. I noticed rainwater flowing down the hillside when the landslide occurred,” Kesavan said. He is undergoing treatment at the Mettupalayam Government Hospital.

Rescue personnel from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) and the Fire and Rescue Services Department rescued Kesavan around 7.30 am on Saturday. Janagaraj was found dead around 11.10 am. He is suspected to have died from a head injury. The bus was severely damaged, with debris entering the vehicle and trapping the two occupants. Rescue teams could not reach the spot immediately as fallen trees and landslide debris blocked the road. They began the operation around 5 am after clearing the obstructions.

Meanwhile, 241 students and 25 teachers from Kerala, who were on a trip to Ooty, were stranded in seven buses due to the disruption of traffic on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road.

**Chennai may receive moderate to heavy rain; red alert issued for Dindigul, Theni, Madurai**

Rescue personnel helped them reach safety, and they were accommodated at marriage halls and a school in Mettupalayam and Kallar. Stranded passengers and drivers were also provided food and medical assistance.

Minister for Backward Classes V Sampath Kumar said the students had been rescued and could retrieve their vehicles once the road was restored and the rain subsided. Later on Saturday evening, the Kerala students were sent back to their native places in buses. Stranded passengers and drivers were also provided with food and medical assistance. Animal Husbandry Minister S Kamali also monitored the rescue and relief work.

Coimbatore Collector Pavankumar G Giriyappanavar said police, revenue, local body and State Highways personnel assisted rescue teams from Mettupalayam, Coonoor, Periyanaickenpalayam, Annur, Kavundampalayam and Sulur.

**IMD alerts, restrictions and wider impact**

The Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai has forecast heavy rain in TN until Monday, as a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a cyclonic storm.

It is very likely to move further northwestwards, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross Andhra Pradesh​ and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam ​by forenoon of October 28. Burliyar in the Nilgiris recorded 25 cm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Saturday, the highest in the state during the period.

Kil Kotagiri Estate received 20 cm, Coonoor 17 cm, Mettupalayam 15 cm and Kotagiri 14 cm. According to TN-SMART data, Virugavoor in the Kallakurichi district recorded a 20 cm of rainfall on Saturday night, while surrounding interior districts registered a lower baseline average of 6.8 mm.

Localised stations within Tiruvannamalai, such as Chengam, separately logged rainfall as high as 11.16 cm. The IMD has issued a red alert for Theni, Dindigul and Madurai districts for Sunday, with extremely heavy rain likely at isolated places. An orange alert is in force for the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Karur, Tiruchy, Nagapattinam, Ariyalur, Perambalur, Sivaganga, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Pudukkottai. Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram and Sivaganga are also under an orange alert for Monday.

Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph are likely at isolated places across TN, Puducherry and Karaikal till Monday. Chennai is likely to receive moderate to heavy rain with thunderstorms on Sunday.

The downpour triggered landslides at 19 locations and tree falls at 18 locations across the Nilgiris. The incident has revived memories of the 1993 Marapalam landslide, when two buses were reportedly buried, killing passengers.

Following the landslides and tree falls, Nilgiris Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Taneeru announced that tourist spots in the district would remain closed until further orders.

She urged tourists to avoid visiting the Nilgiris for the next three days. The district administration has suspended the movement of all vehicles, including TNSTC buses, between 6 pm and 7 am for three days, exempting ambulances and other essential vehicles.

Similar instructions have been issued for Valparai. The Railways has cancelled train services between Mettupalayam and Udhagamandalam on the Nilgiris Mountain Railway for two days following multiple landslides.

A driver travelling in an empty poultry van was also stranded after his vehicle reportedly plunged into a 100-foot gorge during the landslide. He escaped unhurt and returned home.

**Parts of Kodaikanal cut off**

Heavy rain brought parts of Kodaikanal to a standstill on Friday and Saturday, with landslides reported at several locations in Dindigul district. Adukkam panchayat, along the Periyakulam-Kodaikanal route, was cut off after landslides damaged the road at seven locations.

The district administration ordered the closure of tourist spots in Dindigul on Sunday.

A State Highways Department official said the stretch connecting Periyakulam in Theni district and Kodaikanal through Adukkam suffered extensive damage and was closed to traffic on Friday.

# Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

Another wave of landslides and heavy rain has killed about 30 people in Nepal, as the Himalayan nation reels from August's catastrophic flooding that left 1,400 dead and thousands more missing.

The national disaster management authority says more than 1,900 families have been affected since late last week with more than 240 homes damaged. Roads, buildings and bridges have been swept away.

Hundreds of trekkers on the Annapurna Circuit - crucial to Nepal's economy - have had to cut short their hikes to get to safety.

Many have been helicoptered out of the districts of Manang and Mustang, from a hiking circuit that usually takes up to three weeks to complete.

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261019-154138-aa7a263842-web-3.25.0-1/grey-placeholder.png)
![A basic map showing the districts of Mustang and Manang, and how the Annapurna Circuit weaves its way through both of them.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/718f/live/39308b30-bcf8-11f1-babe-4199b0e7ccea.png.webp)

Communities in several parts of Nepal are mourning loved ones.

Speaking from a damp, blue tent in Battar, a town north-west of Kathmandu, Buti Tamang told BBC Nepali: "We used to live in a hut, but now there is nothing. We have lost so many of our relatives."

"Now it is raining and the tent leaks, so we've been facing a difficult situation. We have nowhere to go," said Ramesh Ghale, who also had to flee his home.

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261019-154138-aa7a263842-web-3.25.0-1/grey-placeholder.png)
![Reuters Blue disaster-relief tents on a muddy, forested hillside. A person holding an umbrella stands outside one of the tents. White Chinese characters and a relief-aid logo are visible on the bright blue tent walls.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/4a1a/live/465fa070-bce9-11f1-a64c-550be9e3c66b.jpg.webp)

Several trekkers and their guides say their journeys back down the mountains have been treacherous, taking up to three or four days and requiring them to pass collapsed roads and swept-away bridges.

Jake Stacy, a 21-year-old from Suffolk, found himself stranded with his guide in Yak Kharka, upper Manang, due to heavy snowfall last week and decided not to continue to the Thorang La pass, the highest point of the circuit.

"We made our own paths on mountain slopes," he said, after returning to base camp in Pokhara on Tuesday night. "It was quite steep and we were clambering because there was river below… It was very muddy and very wet.

"Many trekkers were helicoptered out," he added.

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261019-154138-aa7a263842-web-3.25.0-1/grey-placeholder.png)
![Jake Stacy Jake Stacy and his Nepalese guide stand on a snow-covered mountain trail holding trekking poles, with steep white slopes rising behind them. A small stone hut partly covered in snow sits to one side of the path, while low clouds and an overcast sky surround the snowy landscape](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/990c/live/a2de3730-bce9-11f1-8ce2-417f8f7cb095.jpg.webp)

Australian Andrew Graham and his guide Prem KC said they had to cross more than 15 landslides after they decided to return from Manang village. "A few of them were quite dangerous, the residual risks have grown now."

The two got stuck when they reached the village of Chame, which had been evacuated due to the risk of landslides, and had to spend a night in the jungle, Graham said.

A massive landslide has partially blocked a river which passes through Chame, causing a temporary lake that has inundated houses and a key bridge. Authorities have been trying to release the water for the past three days using excavators but have not been very successful, locals told the BBC.

Meanwhile, trekking guide Tse Ring Doma said she and her group had to cross 28 landslides. The mental stress was more difficult than the physical challenge, she said, given the fresh memory of last month's enormous disaster: "Even thunder would make us run and come out to see if anything was coming our way."

Her client, Norwegian Ellen Wahlström, said visitors were fortunate - they would only have to leave some of their items behind, while locals risked losing their houses and land. She added that authorities had been clearing many of the landslides "surprisingly fast".

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261019-154138-aa7a263842-web-3.25.0-1/grey-placeholder.png)
![Jake Stacy Hikers carrying large backpacks and trekking poles climb across a muddy, debris-strewn slope in a dense mountain forest. The trail appears damaged by a landslide, with exposed earth, rocks and uprooted vegetation.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/164d/live/46072ac0-bcea-11f1-a64c-550be9e3c66b.jpg.webp)

While road damage in Manang has been serious, with several bridges swept away and communications down in some areas, no one had been killed in the trekking region, chief district officer Mukti Prasad Khanal said.

But [four bodies have been recovered and 12 people remain missing after an avalanche near the base of Himlung Peak](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwjdvml9e897o), close to the border with Tibet.

A representative of the local trekking authority, the Annapurna Conservation Area Project, said some 700 trekkers were still waiting in Pokhara to embark on the Annapurna Circuit.

"We have been holding back all these people who want to go to the Annapurna Circuit trek, although we are under pressure from the trekking industry to announce the route open," he said.

Indian visitors who often visit the ancient temple Muktinath on a Hindu pilgrimage had been asked to fly from Jomson to Pokhara instead of drive down, due to a cut-off road, he added.

Most of the old trekking trails on the Annapurna Circuit have been unused in recent years after the introduction of roads, except for small pockets of Manang and Mustang districts.

But now operators say many trekkers have been using these abandoned paths to return, as the main roads have been washed away in some sections of the circuit.

results.content:
## Fuel: A lifeline for hospitals

Taiz’s hospitals depend heavily on diesel-powered generators because much of the city’s electricity infrastructure was destroyed during the war that began 11 years ago and has not been restored.

The renewed Houthi siege has severely disrupted the entry of fuel, including the diesel needed to run hospital generators and lifesaving medical equipment.

Dr Shaheed al-Ameri, deputy director-general for technical affairs at the Republican Hospital, said the shortages have had a devastating impact on medical services. [...] The shortages are not confined to the Republican Hospital. On October 22, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned that critical shortages of fuel, oxygen, medicines and medical supplies were threatening lifesaving healthcare throughout  Taiz governorate, with some hospital services already disrupted.

According to the WHO, 42 health facilities in Taiz city had reported severe shortages of essential supplies. Hospitals and ambulances require at least 156,000 litres of fuel a month to continue functioning.

Advertisement

The organisation also warned that diesel shortages threaten to disrupt oxygen production, water pumping, vaccine refrigeration and sanitation services, increasing the risks of disease outbreaks, particularly among displaced families and other vulnerable groups. [...] “Most hospitals have already suspended services in some units because of the shortage of diesel and the lack of necessary medical solutions, as well as shortages of medical staff who are struggling to get to work because of the lack of transport,” he added.

He warned that if conditions continued to deteriorate at the same pace, some hospitals could stop providing services in the coming days.

At the Republican Hospital, al-Ameri said that shortages were also affecting diagnostics and treatment. The availability of laboratory reagents had fallen to just 10 to 15 percent of previous levels, he said, while approximately half of the medicines normally available were now out of stock.

# Hospital in Yemen’s Taiz warns of collapse in days because of Houthi siege

*Dialysis patients face shorter treatment sessions as severe shortages of fuel, medicines, and oxygen threaten hospitals in besieged Yemeni city.*

Save

Share

![Smoke billows from a site that was targeted during battles between Saudi-backed Yemeni government fighters and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis at the Jabal Han front, west of the city of Taiz, on October 21, 2026.](/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/afp_6adb9b137002-1792776979.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)

Signs of battles between Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthis west of Taiz on Wednesday [AFP]

[![](/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/صورتي100-1767530986.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/abdulhakim-helal)

By [AbdulHakim Helal](/author/abdulhakim-helal)

Published On 24 Oct 202624 Oct 2026

**Taiz, Yemen –** It was approaching 10:30am in the dialysis centre of the Republican Hospital in Taiz when a machine began filtering excess fluids, toxins and salts from the blood of Omar Mukhtar Hammoud.

The 16-year-old suffers from kidney failure and is one of 270 patients who regularly receive dialysis at the centre in the government-held city in southwest Yemen. But with essential medical supplies and fuel running critically low under the [renewed Houthi siege](/news/2026/10/10/yemens-taiz-under-siege-again-as-food-and-fuel-prices-rise), doctors fear they may soon be unable to provide the treatment that keeps their patients alive.

## Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

* list 1 of 3[European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks](/news/2026/10/23/european-middle-east-ministers-urge-us-iran-diplomacy-not-new-attacks)
* list 2 of 3[US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February](/news/2026/10/23/us-iran-war-then-and-now-how-the-landscape-has-changed-since-february)
* list 3 of 3[Saudi Arabia security puts Asian Cup in doubt: Japan football chief](/sports/2026/10/23/saudi-arabia-security-puts-asian-cup-in-doubt-japan-football-chief)

end of list

Dr Essam Mahyoub Dahan, the centre’s director, warned that [a complete shutdown](/news/2026/10/11/taiz-hospitals-near-collapse-as-houthis-tighten-siege-yemen-government) could happen within days.

“Because of the siege and the shortage of diesel and medical solutions, we have recently been forced to reduce dialysis sessions from four hours to just two and a half,” Dahan told Al Jazeera. “We know this is not adequate, but we have no choice if we are to keep the centre operating for as long as possible before it shuts down completely.”

Dahan said the centre’s remaining stocks of specialised dialysis solutions were also close to running out.

The supplies, which are expensive, are normally provided by the Yemeni Ministry of Health every three months. But the latest delivery which was due earlier this month  failed to arrive because of the Houthi siege on Taiz city. It began in the first week of October after Houthi advances in the Taiz countryside.

The city was previously under complete Houthi siege between 2015 and 2016, in the early years of Yemen’s ongoing war.

Advertisement

Across Taiz governorate, where battles are raging between the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Iranian-allied Houthi fighters, the number of patients at risk is far greater.

In an October 12 statement, the governorate’s health office warned that the continued siege and obstruction of essential supplies could endanger the lives of 1,110 patients with kidney failure. They depend on dialysis services in the governorate’s hospitals, which collectively provide about 210 dialysis sessions a day.

International humanitarian and health organisations have issued similar warnings about the impact of the siege on the already fragile healthcare system in Taiz.

On Thursday, Amnesty International called on the Houthis to immediately reopen vital roads into and around the city, warning that the closure of the main road between Taiz and the southern port city of Aden threatened hundreds of thousands of civilians with losing access to food, water and healthcare.

## Fuel: A lifeline for hospitals

Taiz’s hospitals depend heavily on diesel-powered generators because much of the city’s electricity infrastructure was destroyed during the war that began 11 years ago and has not been restored.

The renewed Houthi siege has severely disrupted the entry of fuel, including the diesel needed to run hospital generators and lifesaving medical equipment.

Dr Shaheed al-Ameri, deputy director-general for technical affairs at the Republican Hospital, said the shortages have had a devastating impact on medical services.

“A very large part of this suffering is because of the shortage of diesel,” he told Al Jazeera. “We have no reserve diesel supplies. Our stocks ran out early in the siege and we are now buying it on the black market almost every day, at prices that have reached five times what they were before the siege.”

Al-Ameri warned that the longer the siege continues, the more prices will rise and the further medical services will deteriorate.

The hospital has already suspended operations in some departments, including essential units, he said.

“If this situation continues much longer, we fear we will reach a complete and comprehensive collapse of healthcare services,” he said.

The shortages are not confined to the Republican Hospital. On October 22, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned that critical shortages of fuel, oxygen, medicines and medical supplies were threatening lifesaving healthcare throughout  Taiz governorate, with some hospital services already disrupted.

According to the WHO, 42 health facilities in Taiz city had reported severe shortages of essential supplies. Hospitals and ambulances require at least 156,000 litres of fuel a month to continue functioning.

Advertisement

The organisation also warned that diesel shortages threaten to disrupt oxygen production, water pumping, vaccine refrigeration and sanitation services, increasing the risks of disease outbreaks, particularly among displaced families and other vulnerable groups.

The United Nations has separately warned that the restrictions on supplies are bringing Taiz’s health system close to collapse and urged the Houthis to allow humanitarian assistance and essential goods to enter without obstruction.

## Oxygen shortages deepen crisis

In its October 12 statement, Taiz’s health office warned that continued restrictions on fuel deliveries could lead to the shutdown of medical oxygen production plants, further endangering patients.

Taysir al-Samei, the health office’s media officer, said that would dramatically worsen the crisis.

“Many medical departments depend on oxygen, particularly operating theatres, inpatient wards, intensive care units and incubators for premature babies,” al-Samei said.

“Most hospitals have already suspended services in some units because of the shortage of diesel and the lack of necessary medical solutions, as well as shortages of medical staff who are struggling to get to work because of the lack of transport,” he added.

He warned that if conditions continued to deteriorate at the same pace, some hospitals could stop providing services in the coming days.

At the Republican Hospital, al-Ameri said that shortages were also affecting diagnostics and treatment. The availability of laboratory reagents had fallen to just 10 to 15 percent of previous levels, he said, while approximately half of the medicines normally available were now out of stock.

Prices for the remaining medicines had doubled, he said, placing them further out of reach for patients already struggling with Yemen’s worsening economic crisis.

The continued fighting and shelling around Taiz have increased the number of wounded people requiring emergency care – placing additional pressure on facilities already struggling with [shortages of surgical supplies](/news/2026/10/14/renewed-fighting-risks-humanitarian-catastrophe-in-yemen-aid-groups-warn), anaesthetics and intravenous fluids.

Abdul Badi Abdulwuhab, 53, is another dialysis patient in the Republican Hospital, struggling to cope with the shorter dialysis sessions.

His voice was filled with desperation.

“Because of these measures, I suffer from weakness and I cannot bear the pain,” Abdul Badi told Al Jazeera. “Two and a half hours is not enough to remove all the fluids and toxins from my body.”

Dr Dahan said that the patient’s condition had deteriorated since his sessions were shortened.

“These measures are not effective for many patients,” Dahan said. “The only solution is to end the siege and return things to the way they were.”
